skill.name: fatigue-frequency-manager
skill.description: Analyzes paid ad frequency, CTR, CVR, and reach trends against an early-flight baseline. Returns a rotate-creative, widen-audience, or hold recommendation for each ad set.
skill.summary: Diagnoses ad creative fatigue and audience saturation from campaign trend data.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown backticks, repository URLs, and relative documentation links. One medium-risk command-use finding is confirmed because SKILL.md instructs running ledger.py with an ad-set argument that can originate from user input. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unauthorized network behavior was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Command invocation with user-controlled ad-set names
remediation.suggestion: Document that ledger.py must be invoked with argument arrays or safely quoted values, and validate ad-set names before passing them to any shell command.

remediation.issue: Potential confusion between documentation links and file access
remediation.suggestion: Keep relative markdown links as documentation only, and state that the skill must not read arbitrary paths supplied by exported campaign data.

content.value_statement: Scaling ad sets can lose performance when frequency rises and CTR or CVR decays. This skill turns campaign trend exports into clear rotate, widen, or hold decisions.
actual_capabilities: Compares current ad frequency, CTR, CVR, and reach against an early-flight baseline.
Separates creative fatigue from audience saturation using reach and frequency trends.
Returns one rotate-creative, widen-audience, or hold trigger for each ad set.
Flags CVR drops that may reflect broken tracking or double-counted conversions.
Creates a concise handoff summary for saved campaign review notes.
limitations: Requires a daily or weekly time series; a single-day snapshot is not enough.
Does not create replacement ads or creative concepts.
Does not compute the full RQS score or run final account vetoes.
Optional platform APIs are convenience inputs, not required integrations.

use_cases.title: Review Scaling Prospecting Sets
use_cases.description: Check whether rising frequency and falling CTR mean the ad needs fresh creative or a larger audience.

use_cases.title: Separate Fatigue From Tracking Noise
use_cases.description: Compare platform CVR drops with analytics or store data before acting on a conversion decline.

use_cases.title: Create Clear Optimization Handovers
use_cases.description: Summarize the baseline, trend, trigger, and caveats so another teammate can act on the decision.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Ad Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with a simple export.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this daily export for Ad Set A. Tell me whether frequency and CTR show fatigue, saturation, or no clear issue.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Several Ad Sets
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these ad sets against their early-flight baselines. Return one rotate, widen, or hold trigger for each set.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a CVR Drop
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review when conversion quality may be unreliable.
prompt_templates.prompt: CTR is falling and CVR also dropped. Compare the platform export with GA4 and store orders before recommending any action.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Decision Handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for saved campaign notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a handoff summary with baseline window, current frequency, CTR slope, CVR slope, reach trend, trigger, threshold, and caveats.

output_examples.input: Ad Set A shows frequency 6.2, CTR down 48 percent, reach still growing, and CVR stable.
output_examples.output: Trigger: Rotate creative. The pattern points to creative fatigue because CTR declined while reach continued to expand and CVR stayed stable.

output_examples.input: Ad Set B shows reach plateaued, frequency rising each week, CTR down 31 percent, and CVR down 18 percent.
output_examples.output: Trigger: Widen audience. The main signal is saturation because reach stopped expanding while frequency increased and both click and conversion rates weakened.

output_examples.input: Ad Set C has one dashboard screenshot with yesterday's frequency and CTR only.
output_examples.output: Trigger: Hold. A fatigue read needs a time series and a stable baseline, so the current data is not enough for a decision.

best_practices: Use a stable early-flight baseline after the learning phase ends.
Label every metric as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Confirm conversion drops against analytics or order data before acting.
anti_patterns: Calling fatigue from one day of dashboard data.
Using one universal frequency ceiling for every campaign objective.
Rotating creative when the real issue is broken conversion tracking.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs a time series with impressions, reach, frequency, clicks or CTR, spend, and conversions or CVR when available.

faq.question: Can it work without CVR?
faq.answer: Yes. It can read a creative fatigue signal from CTR and frequency, but it will mark CVR as unavailable.

faq.question: Does it build replacement creative?
faq.answer: No. It diagnoses whether creative should rotate, then hands that task to a creative building workflow.

faq.question: Does it connect directly to ad platforms?
faq.answer: No direct API is required. Manual exports are supported, and optional connectors are only convenience inputs.

faq.question: How does it avoid false fatigue calls?
faq.answer: It compares trends against a baseline and checks whether reach, frequency, CTR, and CVR tell the same story.

faq.question: Can it save results?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks before saving a scoped handoff note for later campaign review.
